{"id": "85275710-22c5-4fdf-9283-ee62a3914f94", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Here's my read on this advanced selector, no account access needed — straight logic analysis.

**How it evaluates per bucket**

All four `FieldSelectors` are ANDed within the one selector (`"s3 writes"`), so an event is only logged if it satisfies every condition simultaneously.

| Bucket | PutObject / DeleteObject logged? | Other object events (GetObject, CopyObject, DeleteObjects, PutObjectTagging, PutObjectAcl, multipart completes, etc.) |
|---|---|---|
| **scratch-bucket** | ❌ No — `resources.ARN` starts with `[redacted ARN]`, fails the `NotStartsWith` condition, so it's excluded from this selector entirely | ❌ No — would also fail the explicit exclusion, and wouldn't match `eventName` anyway |
| **finance-bucket** | ✅ Yes — ARN doesn't match the excluded prefix | ❌ No — `eventName Equals [PutObject, DeleteObject]` only matches those two API calls |
| **hr-bucket** | ✅ Yes | ❌ No — same reason |

The `[redacted ARN]` exclusion correctly includes the trailing slash, so it only excludes scratch-bucket's own objects — it won't accidentally catch a bucket like `scratch-bucket-prod`. That part is well-scoped.

**Gaps worth flagging in the audit**

1. **"s3 writes" undercounts actual writes.** The selector only catches `PutObject` and `DeleteObject`. It misses other mutating object-level calls on finance-bucket and hr-bucket: `DeleteObjects` (bulk/batch delete — commonly used by lifecycle jobs and scripts), `CopyObject`, `CompleteMultipartUpload`/`UploadPart` (large-file uploads), `PutObjectTagging`, `PutObjectAcl`, `RestoreObject`, and `PostObject` (browser form uploads). A bulk delete via `DeleteObjects` on hr-bucket or finance-bucket today would produce **zero CloudTrail record**, despite the selector's name suggesting "writes" are covered.
2. **No read visibility.** By design, `GetObject`/`HeadObject` aren't covered — fine if the audit scope is write-only, but worth stating explicitly since the two sensitive buckets (finance, hr) have no object-read audit trail from this selector.
3. **scratch-bucket is fully dark for S3 data events.** Not just Put/Delete — since it's excluded at the ARN level, even if you later widen `eventName`, scratch-bucket stays excluded. If scratch-bucket is ever used for anything beyond disposable data, there's currently zero data-event visibility into it.
4. **This selector only speaks to object-level data events.** It says nothing about whether this trail also logs S3 **management**-category events (e.g., `PutBucketPolicy`, `PutBucketAcl`, `CreateBucket`, `PutBucketVersioning`) — those come from a separate selector/category and aren't shown here, so I can't confirm bucket-level config changes are captured.

**Net rating:** This selector does what it says for `PutObject`/`DeleteObject` specifically, correctly isolates finance-bucket and hr-bucket from scratch-bucket — but the name "s3 writes" overstates its coverage. I'd call it **partial write coverage**, not full, due to the missing `DeleteObjects`, `CopyObject`, and ACL/tagging/multipart operations.

If you want, I can also check whether a management-event selector exists on this trail, or draft the additional `eventName` values needed to close the bulk-delete/copy gap.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
